newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's WestLB to introduce OTC currency options.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's WestLB to introduce OTC currency options.

text.p: Westdeutsche Landesbank Hungaria Rt (WestLB) wishes to play a pioneering role next year when it launches OTC currency options for what it describes as its strategic clients, bank officials said on Friday.

"According to our best information there's no commercial bank in Hungary now which would continously offer ...currency options in dollar/forint, mark/forint or any other currency/forint," said Geza Egyed, head of treasury at WestLB.
From January 1997 the bank will offer European style OTC currency options for dollar/forint and mark/forint for maturities up to three months, he told a news conference.
The European style options can be called or put at expiry only, unlike the American style options which could be called or put at any time.
At the beginning WestLB will limit its deals at $2 million because the bank will have only limited opportunities to hedge its own risks.
The bank (WestLB) has to hedge an option deal on the underlying market because, for the time being, there's no other bank which would share our risk, Egyed said.
Options markets practically do not exist in Hungary, although both the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) and the Budapest Commodity Exchange plan to launch standardised options markets.
The BSE has had a traditional options market for stocks but suspended its operations for an indefinite period due to insufficient regulation.

However, both the BSE and the BCE have standardised currency futures markets. The BCE offers Swiss francs, sterling, Italian lira and yen, in addition to dollar, mark and Ecu contracts which are also offered on the BSE.
